relevance_note: Case report of one adult with a heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant diagnosed with HA20 ("The results revealed a heterozygous variant of the TNFAIP3 gene, specifically c.259C>T (R87X)"), plus a literature table (Table 2) of 11 published HA20 patients with CNS involvement.
method_note: Read in full by hand; a short script copied Table 2 cells and built row-prefix spans, and every transcribed value was asserted equal to its table cell. Scope: the proband (II-3; also Table 2 row 1 'Our case', not duplicated), three relatives with oral ulcers named in the pedigree (II-2, III-1, III-3; untested, no variant rows), and Table 2 cases 2-12 (previously published, source_reference_in_review = Table 2 Reference cell). Labels: Table 2 'No.' column gives 'Table 2 #n'; cases 11 and 12 are called 'cases 11 and 12' / 'case 12' in the text, so rule 1 gives 'case 11' and 'case 12'. Table 2 zygosity from its note 'The genotype of all cases was heterozygous.' (named group = all Table 2 cases). Table 2 disease label from 'Table 2 shows characteristics of only HA20 patients'. Table 2 case 5 'Current treatment' cell reads 'Died' -> vital_status deceased; its 'Current age' 8 years recorded as last evaluation; age at death not stated. Case 5 ethnicity printed 'unknown (adopted)' -> not reported. Case 5 'frontal lobe punctate' is an incomplete phrase and was not recorded as a feature. Proband: NLRP3 c.214G>A and PLCG2 c.1959C>T (Table 1) are common in Japanese (ToMMo AF 1.011e-2, 3.266e-2) and 'assessed to have limited disease relevance', so no rows were made for them. RELA testing found no variants. Contradictions/inconsistencies: (1) proband onset: Table 2 gives '18 years' (recorded), but the text says 'recurrent oral ulcers since 10 years of age' and a history of symptoms at 28 years; (2) Figure 2 legend writes 'c.159C>T' for R87X while text and Table 1 give c.259C>T (recorded); protein printed as p.Arg87Ter (Table 1), p.Arg87* (Table 2) and R87X (text); (3) 'He had no family history of autoimmune or autoinflammatory diseases' versus later relatives with oral ulcers after the family history was re-evaluated; relatives recorded from the later statement. Age at diagnosis of HA20 not stated (incomplete Behcet disease diagnosed at 28 years is a different diagnosis), left not reported. Neurological examination at admission was 'unremarkable, with no evidence of diplopia' (transient symptom; not recorded as excluded). Gastrointestinal endoscopy excluded only 'gastrointestinal ulcers', so the composite checklist item is not reported; 'no new shadows or pleural effusion' excludes pleural effusion only, so serositis is not reported. 'Suspected atypical mycobacterial infection' was hedged and tests were negative; recurrent infections left not reported. Liver dysfunction absent does not exclude autoimmune hepatitis. No stacked cells in this paper.

study_type.span: Title: Case report: Adult case of A20 haploinsufficiency suspected as neuro-Behçet disease

n_patients_reported.span: Here, we describe a patient with HA20

treatment_summary.value: colchicine and low-dose prednisolone (0-5 mg/day, self-increased to 6-10 mg/day); PSL 20 mg for sensorineural hearing loss, tapered; methotrexate 12 mg/week with poor response; adalimumab, after which oral ulcers disappeared and inflammatory signs became negative; colchicine discontinued owing to diarrhea; prednisolone tapered to 2 mg/day
span: He had been self-administering colchicine and low-dose prednisolone (PSL) at a dosage of 0–5 mg/day for oral and genital ulcers
he self-increased his dosage of PSL to 6–10 mg/day
started PSL at a dosage of 20 mg, which resulted in an improvement in hearing. The PSL dosage was tapered to 5 mg.
the patient received an increased dosage of PSL and additional treatment with methotrexate (12 mg/week), but he showed a poor therapeutic response

After starting adalimumab, the oral ulcers disappeared, inflammatory signs became negative for the first time, and there were no episodes of diplopia thereafter. Colchicine was discontinued owing to diarrhea, and tapering of prednisolone to a dosage of 2 mg/day became possible

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: gene panel testing for hereditary autoinflammatory diseases found a heterozygous TNFAIP3 c.259C>T variant, previously reported in HA20; NF-kB reporter functional analysis; diagnosis of HA20 made on these findings
span: A gene panel test for periodic fever syndromes revealed a variant in the TNFAIP3 gene, showing a c.259C>T nonsense variant. As previous reports have described the same variant in patients with HA20, the patient was diagnosed with HA20.

The R87X variant identified in this case exhibited considerably higher luciferase activity than the wild-type, indicating a pathological variant with impaired inhibition of NF-κB activity. On the basis of these findings, the patient was diagnosed with HA20.
